jurisdiction.name: Angola
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Angola has no adopted AI law or AI strategy. Its ICT White Paper 2023-2027, approved by Presidential Decree 272/24, commits to a national AI strategy, a National AI Council, AI ethics guidelines and an annual AI readiness index. A draft AI Law (2025), a draft revision of the data protection law with AI rules (2025) and a draft Digital Government Law with public-sector AI rules (2026) are all still drafts; the 2011 data protection law remains in force. Law 6/26 of August 2026 against false information online is reported to define deepfakes and AI bots.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication (MINTTICS)
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: Law 6/26 of 4 August 2026 against false information online; the national AI strategy (in preparation); the public-sector digital governance and AI framework (in preparation). Official sources checked on 12 and 13 October 2026 include official gazette copies, Parliament, the government and each ministry and sector regulator; the official gazette's own website and the websites of the defence and agriculture ministries and of the media, competition and standards bodies were unreachable.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication (MINTTICS), as proponent
instruments.current_status: Draft bill dated 'Luanda, Setembro de 2025' published for public consultation on the MINTTICS consultation portal (consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao), where it remains the only document in consultation; the portal does not state opening/closing dates. No submission to the National Assembly and no gazette publication found as of 13 October 2026.
instruments.summary: A 86-article draft general AI law proposed by MINTTICS, preceded by a justification report with a comparative study (US, EU, China, Japan, Canada, Brazil, Africa). It sets AI principles, user rights (information, explanation and refusal of AI-based decisions, complaints), safety, risk-assessment, incident-reporting and AI-content labelling duties for developers and providers, a stricter regime for 'critical AI' (registration, risk assessment, emergency response), and special rules for AI use by the State and public administration, judicial, news and medical AI, social bots, biometric recognition, autonomous driving and general-purpose AI. It provides for an AI competent authority to be created by regulation, an expert commission, administrative offences, AI crimes, strict civil liability and pilot supervision mechanisms.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Angola's first draft horizontal AI law; would create a dedicated AI regulator.

instruments.english_title: Draft Revision of Law No. 22/11 of 17 June - Personal Data Protection Law (public-consultation version)
instruments.issuing_authority: Data Protection Agency (Agência de Protecção de Dados, APD)
instruments.current_status: Put to public consultation by the APD on the government consultation portal from 17 March to 17 April 2025 (status 'Encerrada'). Not adopted as of 13 October 2026 (no gazette publication found); Law 22/11 remains in force.
instruments.summary: Draft replacement of Angola's 2011 data protection law put to consultation by the APD. Besides a right not to be subject to solely automated or semi-automated decisions, it adds a section on processing personal data by AI systems: it bans AI that manipulates people into compromising privacy, exploits vulnerabilities of specific groups, or performs social scoring leading to unfavourable treatment. It gives data subjects affected by AI rights to prior information, explanation, contestation and human participation, and requires AI producers, providers and operators to adopt governance and data-management practices against discrimination.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would introduce AI-specific prohibitions and data-subject rights into Angolan data protection law.

instruments.summary: Draft framework law on digital government covering digital public services, electronic administrative procedure, digital identity, public-data governance, interoperability and the use of automated systems and AI in public administration. It subjects public-sector AI to legality, necessity, proportionality, transparency, explainability, non-discrimination, human oversight and accountability, bans AI for indiscriminate mass surveillance, unlawful profiling or arbitrary discrimination, and requires prior impact and risk assessment, an institutional register, technical documentation and audit records for AI used in relevant administrative functions. The administration remains liable for errors caused by data, design, bias or insufficient oversight.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would set binding rules for AI use by Angolan public administration.

instruments.official_title: Lei n.º 22/11, de 17 de Junho - Lei da Protecção de Dados Pessoais
instruments.english_title: Law No. 22/11 of 17 June 2011 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.current_status: In force since publication in Diário da República I Série n.º 114 of 17 June 2011 (art. 67). A full revision prepared by the Data Protection Agency was put to public consultation in March-April 2025 and was not yet adopted as of 13 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Angola's general personal data protection law, applying to wholly or partly automated processing of personal data and supervised by the Data Protection Agency. Its art. 29 gives every person the right not to be subject to a decision producing legal or similarly significant effects based solely on automated processing intended to evaluate personal aspects such as professional capacity, creditworthiness, reliability or conduct, with exceptions for contracts with safeguards and cases authorised by the Agency with safeguards defined by it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only binding Angolan rule found that directly governs automated (algorithmic) decision-making.

instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic (Presidente da República)
instruments.current_status: Approved by Presidential Decree 272/24, published in Diário da República I Série n.º 231 of 5 December 2024 and in force on publication (art. 4); covers 2023-2027. Repeals Presidential Dispatch 129/19 of 22 July 2019 (ICT White Paper 2019-2022) (art. 2). The national AI strategy (ENIA) it announces had not been published as of 13 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Angola's national ICT policy for 2023-2027, approved by presidential decree and steering the telecoms/ICT sector towards a 'Society 5.0'. Its section 9.7.1 on artificial intelligence recognises the need for specific AI legislation and common rules for all AI systems, commits the Executive to design and implement a National AI Strategy (ENIA), and lists lines of action: AI skills and university research, computing capacity, strengthening regulators' capacity and public trust, an annual 'AI Readiness Index', AI in public services (including innovation-friendly procurement from local AI suppliers), a National AI Council, an 'Angola IA' ecosystem programme, and ethical AI development guidelines with a national AI ethics network across government bodies. It also lists a 'Plano Estratégico Nacional de Inteligência Artificial' in its legislative reform programme.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Government-approved policy with an AI pillar; the formal basis for Angola's planned national AI strategy, AI council and AI ethics guidelines.

leads.title: Lei n.º 6/26, de 4 de Agosto - Lei contra Informações Falsas na Internet
leads.english_title: Law No. 6/26 of 4 August 2026 against False Information on the Internet
leads.note: Enacted law (approved 21 May 2026; per its text published in Diário da República I Série n.º 146 of 4 August 2026, in force on publication, art. 31). Defines 'deepfake' (alteration of video or photo with the help of AI), 'artificial disseminators' (bots) and 'artificial dissemination networks', and requires application providers to report monthly to the electronic-communications regulator on artificial disseminators removed and to act against unclassified artificial disseminators. In scope (AI-generated content/bots) but no official copy found: the Imprensa Nacional gazette site was unreachable and the text was not found on parlamento.ao, inacom.gov.ao, minttics.gov.ao or governo.gov.ao; seen only on a private legal database. Promote when an official copy is reachable.
